metadata.title: Entanglement Entropy — The Ebit Curve: Arc Right, Bloch Ball Wrong

beats.narration_text: Kia ora. Liam here. Claude wrote this visualization — three panels, one slider, the full arc of entanglement entropy. Today we judge the viz, not the physics.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for entanglement entropy.
output: ✓ three live panels: S_E curve, Bloch ball, Schmidt bars

beats.narration_text: Three panels, left to right: an entropy curve with a live tracker dot, a Bloch ball for subsystem A, and two Schmidt coefficient bars. One theta slider, zero to forty-five degrees. The readout strip shows theta, both eigenvalues, entropy in ebits, and purity.

As theta sweeps zero to forty-five: the entropy dot climbs the pre-drawn arc — concave, fast near zero, flattening toward Bell. The Bloch dot drops from the pole to center. The bars equalize. At forty-five degrees, one ebit — maximum entanglement, confirmed.

The pre-drawn entropy arc is the standout design choice. Before you drag, you see the whole curve — you form an expectation, the sweep confirms or breaks it. That predict-before-reveal moment is where concept formation happens. Second: three simultaneous panels each translate the same state into a different register. A student who knows entropy cross-checks against the Bloch ball; one who knows Bloch vectors checks against the bars. And the normalization checksum — lambda-one plus lambda-two equals one, running live — turns a textbook constraint into something you can watch.

Three real problems. The Bloch ball's blue disc has no label and no physics name. Its radius grows proportional to the departure from purity, but the code never names that quantity and the disc looks like an uncertainty cloud. A student who knows Bloch spheres is confused; one who doesn't invents an interpretation. Second: switch to asymmetric mode and drag alpha — the readout updates correctly, but the entropy chart cursor freezes. The update block is inside if-mode-equals-symmetric with no else branch. The main visual and the readout silently disagree. Third: reference annotations render at nine pixels and silently drop their S-value line — the markup promises the number, the render call discards it.

Let's recap with Claude. The pre-drawn arc earns its keep — predict-before-reveal is real pedagogy. Three representations is right. The Bloch ball's blue disc is the problem: no label, no physics name, looks like uncertainty where there is none. Fix it first — draw the Bloch vector as a labeled line. The asymmetric mode cursor freeze is a silent bug. Best use: right after Schmidt decomposition, before entropy is a formula.

artifactLines: Pre-drawn arc: prediction visible before dragging
Three panels cross-check the same state in three registers
Bloch ball blue disc: growing, unlabeled, not standard
Asymmetric mode: cursor freezes while readout updates
Best use: after Schmidt decomp, before entropy is defined

beats.narration_text: I have an entanglement entropy visualization with a Bloch ball panel. The ball draws a growing blue disc to show the degree of mixedness — but the disc has no label, no physics name, and isn't standard Bloch sphere convention. Replace it with an explicit Bloch vector: a line from center to the state point, labeled z equals cos two theta. Also fix this bug: in asymmetric mode the entropy chart cursor freezes because the update is inside if-mode-equals-sym with no else branch. Fix both, then add a tooltip on the pre-drawn entropy curve that shows the exact S_E value on hover.
